sections.label: Early Childhood Development Agency established
sections.summary: ECDA was established in 2013 to regulate and develop the sector, and parents of over 165,000 children entrust their children to these centres daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In support of this, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) was established in 2013 to regulate and develop the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Today, parents of over 165,000 children entrust their children to these centres each day.

sections.label: Three-year licence tenure increase
sections.summary: The maximum licence tenure will increase to three years from two for childcare centres, recognising over 500 centres with good track records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Under the new framework, we will increase the maximum licence tenure to three years, up from the current two years for childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The new three-year licence tenure recognises the strong core of centres with consistently good regulatory track records of at least two consecutive two-year licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is a substantial portion of childcare centres, at over 500 centres today.

sections.label: Prohibiting unsuitable persons managing centres
sections.summary: Under clause 19, ECDA will continue to prohibit unsuitable persons, such as those with poor regulatory track records, from managing the centre's business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Under clause 19, ECDA will continue to prohibit unsuitable persons, such as those with poor regulatory track records, from managing the centre's business as board directors or chief executive officers and so on.

sections.label: Daily physical activities in centres
sections.summary: Centres with full-day programmes will need to conduct at least one hour of physical activities daily, half of which outdoors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For example, as announced by the NurtureSG Taskforce last week, centres with full-day programmes will need to conduct at least one hour of physical activities daily, up from half-hour currently, and half-hour of which has to be conducted outdoors.

sections.label: New administrative penalty framework
sections.summary: Administrative lapses will be decriminalised and replaced with administrative regulatory sanctions including public censures, financial penalties, security deposits, remedial measures and shortened licence tenure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With this new penalty framework, administrative lapses will be decriminalised and replaced with administrative regulatory sanctions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This will allow us a wider suite of regulatory sanctions ranging from public censures, administrative financial penalties of up to $5,000, a security deposit, remedial measures and a shortening of licence tenure.

sections.label: Security deposit for poor track records
sections.summary: The security deposit is intended to apply only to centres with poor track records, with a $10,000 amount being considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The current intention is for the security deposit to apply only to the small number of centres with poor track records, such as centres with two consecutive six-month licences, which is the lowest licence standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are also mindful that the security deposit amount should be calibrated appropriately and not be overly onerous on the centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are looking at a $10,000 amount, which is twice the administrative financial penalty amount for contraventions.

sections.label: Penalties for contraventions
sections.summary: The Bill makes such contraventions punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 and/or up to 12 months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Under the Bill, such contraventions will incur a fine of up to $10,000 and/or an imprisonment term of up to 12 months.

sections.label: ECDA officers' search powers
sections.summary: Clause 37 empowers ECDA officers to search centres, interview persons, take photographs and videos, and obtain documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Beyond the current powers to inspect centres, ECDA officers, under clause 37, will be empowered to search centres, interview persons, take photographs and videos of the centre, and obtain the necessary documents from the centre.

sections.label: Kindergarten licensing transition period
sections.summary: Clause 54 gives kindergartens one year from the Act's commencement to obtain their licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As kindergartens are less familiar with a licensing regime, under clause 54 of the Bill, kindergartens will be given one year from the commencement of the Act to obtain their licences.

sections.label: Licensing of all centres
sections.summary: A key provision in the Bill requires all centres to be licensed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One of the key provisions in this Bill is for all centres to be licensed.

sections.label: Childcare fee variation
sections.summary: Fees vary significantly, from over $600 per month to $2,000 per month in high-end childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Right now, the fee variation is significant − from over $600 per month to $2,000 per month in high-end childcare centres.

sections.label: Childcare fees and subsidies
sections.summary: From 2011 to 2015 the median full-time childcare fee rose 25%, while middle-income family subsidy stayed at $300 since 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2015, the median fee of a full-time childcare centre has increased 25%, but the subsidy given to middle-income families has remained at $300 since 2008.

sections.label: Obesity rise in school children
sections.summary: Recent studies show obesity in school children rose from 10% in 2000 to 12% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Recent studies show that obesity in school children has risen from 10% in 2000 to 12% in 2014.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: A parent supports the Bill, saying it formalises existing practices and opens up preschool sector possibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the above suggestions, the Bill is important and critical for nurturing the next generation of younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am thus speaking from the point of view as a parent and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, the proposed legislation would formalise many of the existing good regulatory practices that are already in place and tweak some to maintain a good balance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, and more importantly today, the proposed legislation opens up the possibilities of developing the preschool sector.

sections.label: ECDA regulating curriculum
sections.summary: ECDA will be empowered to regulate the curriculum of childcare centres and kindergartens under the licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first is the potential of enhancing innovation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is good that ECDA will be empowered to regulate the curriculum of childcare centres and kindergartens under the licensing regime.

sections.label: Fear of higher fees
sections.summary: A main fear is that increased regulatory and compliance costs would be passed to parents through higher fees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One of the main fears related to this legislation is the increase of regulatory and compliance costs that would be passed on to parents through increased fees.

sections.label: Reviewing subsidy eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Regulatory costs present an opportunity to review subsidies, including basing eligibility on four or more family members.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, there will be some regulatory costs and knock-on effects on fees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This, therefore, presents the Government with the opportunity to review its subsidy schemes, especially with the view of ensuring low-income families can afford preschool education for their children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first is for the per capita income eligibility criteria for the Additional Infant and Child Care Subsidies and the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme to be based on four or more family members in the same household, including at least two dependants, rather than on the existing five or more family members with more than two dependants.

sections.label: KiFAS for POP and VWO kindergartens
sections.summary: KiFAS subsidies would be opened to eligible parents of children in kindergartens run by Partner Operators and voluntary welfare organisations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second is to open up Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) subsidies to eligible parents of children enrolled in kindergartens operated by Partner Operators (POPs) and voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs).

sections.label: Kindergarten and childcare enrolment shifts
sections.summary: Kindergarten enrolment fell about 6% and kindergartens dropped from 500 to 480, while childcare enrolment rose about 50% and infant care rose 60% since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, it was noted that over the past three years, kindergarten enrolment dropped by about 6% and the number of kindergartens dropped from 500 to 480.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the other hand, childcare enrolment shot up by about 50%, from 76,000 to about 100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Since 2012, the number of infants enrolled in infant care has increased by 60%, now accounting for about 10% of the infants.

sections.label: Section 17 penalties for licensees
sections.summary: Section 17 sets directions on children's safety and well-being, with non-compliant licensees fined up to $10,000 or jailed up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 17 spells out the directions concerning the safety and well-being of children.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, the licensee who fails to comply will be imposed a fine of up to $10,000 or not exceeding 12 months' imprisonment.

sections.label: Concerns on smaller niche centres
sections.summary: The speaker does not oppose the Bill's intent but questions specific provisions and implementation, concerned about smaller centres offering niche services such as to children with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While I do not oppose the intent of this Bill, I shall raise questions about specific provisions and its implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am concerned about the status of smaller centres that may offer niche services, for example, to children with special needs.

sections.label: Dr Aline Wong on preschool diversity
sections.summary: Dr Aline Wong in 2000 said different preschool providers offer a wide range of models, promoting competition and innovation, and the speaker asks if the Ministry expects major consolidation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, in the year 2000, Dr Aline Wong, then Senior Minister of State for Education, said and I quote, "Today, different preschool providers with their different philosophies and approaches to child development offer a wide range of preschool education models in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is merit in this arrangement as it promotes healthy competition and provides a fertile arena for innovative practices." I would like to ask the Ministry: does it expect a major consolidation in the industry as a result of this Bill?

sections.label: Exemption for MOE kindergartens
sections.summary: The speaker says, as Assoc Prof Daniel Goh argued, the exemption for MOE kindergartens is hard to accept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, as my colleague Assoc Prof Daniel Goh has argued, the exemption for MOE kindergartens is hard to accept.

sections.label: Singapore's preschool quality and affordability ranking
sections.summary: The same well-known report ranked Singapore 30th globally in preschool education quality and 21st in affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The same well-known report placed Singapore 30th in the global ranking of preschool education quality, and 21st in terms of affordability.

sections.label: Free childcare and absenteeism study
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will explore free kindergarten and childcare for at-risk poor children and study absenteeism tied to subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Sweden, all children receive at least 525 hours per year free of charge, beginning from when the child reaches the age of three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the longer term, and as a first step, will the Ministry explore the idea of making a more aggressive financial intervention to provide free, good quality kindergarten and childcare to all at-risk children in poor families, perhaps tied to certain conditions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, there is anecdotal evidence that children from many poor, low-income families sometimes attend kindergartens or childcare centres only a few times a month which is the minimum to continue receiving the KiFAS or Cebtre-based Financial Assistance for Childcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry conduct a study of this absenteeism phenomenon and also consider policies to address this?

sections.label: Co-locating primary schools and childcare
sections.summary: Suggests ECDA work with MOE to co-locate primary schools and childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, I would like to suggest that ECDA works with MOE to co-locate primary schools and childcare centres.

sections.label: Training more early childhood educators
sections.summary: Notes educator training requirements and asks whether a new institution could train more early childhood educators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Early childhood educators must attend an ECDA-recognised course or diploma programme conducted at ITEs, polytechnics or ECDA-accredited training agencies, such as the SEED Institute or MMI Academy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To further alleviate the shortage of childcare staff, can the Ministry consider setting up a new institution to train more early childhood educators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I observe that currently, childcare staff is relatively young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will be a win-win situation as it will help alleviate the manpower shortage faced by childcare centres, as well as help our middle-aged workers.

sections.label: Licensing third-party education providers
sections.summary: Proposes that third-party education providers be licensed so centres can choose from a list of licensed providers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, for a centre to engage a third-party education provider, it is mandatory to apply to the Chief Licensing Officer (CLO).

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I propose that third-party education providers should also be licensed, and the centres can then take their pick from a list of the licensed providers at any given time.

sections.label: Reviewing childcare teacher salaries
sections.summary: States that a longer-term solution to the manpower crunch is reviewing childcare teachers' salaries, especially the disparity with MOE teachers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of course, a longer-term solution to the manpower crunch is to review the salaries of childcare teachers, especially the disparity with MOE teachers.

sections.label: Simpler rules for their well-being
sections.summary: Requests adequate regulations to protect well-being, health and safety, and a simpler set of rules for them.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There must be adequate regulations to protect their well-being, health and safety.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I request that while they do not need to comply with all the rules in this Bill, the Government should look into a simpler set of rules for them.

sections.label: Childcare centres and infant care
sections.summary: Singapore has over 1,300 childcare centres, with close to 500 offering infant care services at the same premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, there are over 1,300 childcare centres in Singapore, with close to 500 of them offering infant care services at the same premises.

sections.label: Operators with ill practices
sections.summary: Under this Bill, operators with ill practices will either shape up or exit the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, operators with ill practices will either shape up or exit the market.

sections.label: Whistle-blowers and unpaid wages
sections.summary: A Member asks if the Ministry will encourage whistle-blowers to share insights on ill practices and give the agency more muscle to compel operators to comply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider having measures to encourage whistle-blowers from among the centres to come forward and share their insights if they know of any ill practices?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know of operators who have been cited by the authorities to pay staff who are owed wages but they have been uncooperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope the regulatory agency will be given more muscle to compel the operators to comply, rather than having the staff to resort to filing civil claims.

sections.label: Single framework for preschools
sections.summary: Regulating childcare centres and kindergartens under a single framework ensures consistency in enforcement of standards and operational requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Regulating childcare centres and kindergartens under a single framework ensures consistency in the enforcement of standards and other operational requirements.

sections.label: Accessible locations for preschool centres
sections.summary: Preschool centres should be at accessible venues, with better advance planning so new childcare centres and BTO flats are built almost simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, important for our preschool centres to be located at accessible and convenient venues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There can be better planning in advance so that the building of new childcare centres and new BTO flats can take place almost simultaneously.

sections.label: Coordination on childcare and BTO flats
sections.summary: Building childcare centres alongside BTO flats ensures convenience for senior citizens, and the Member hopes for coordination between MND and MSF on childcare vacancies and physical activity facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: By building the new childcare centres alongside the BTO HDB flats, it will ensure convenience for these senior citizens who would otherwise have to walk long distances or take public transport with the children to and from the centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope for a greater degree of coordination between the Ministry of National Development, including agencies like HDB, and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), so that the issue of childcare vacancies does not burden parents, especially when we want to encourage young parents to consider having another child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given the new recommendation by the NutureSG Committee for preschool children to have at least one hour of physical activity per day, incorporating facilities within the childcare centre to enable this would be essential.

sections.label: Cost impact of new regulations
sections.summary: Asks whether operating centre costs will rise with compliance and if the Ministry has an indicator of the impact on existing and new centres.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Will the cost of operating a centre increase in tandem with the need to comply with these new regulations?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have an indicator of the impact these new rules will have on our existing centres and the new centres to be built?

sections.label: Qualification criteria for non-teaching staff
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider different qualification criteria for non-teaching staff using relevant experience instead of ECDA recognised educator certifications.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider different sets of qualification criteria for non-teaching staff where relevant experience, rather than ECDA's recognised educator certifications are being used?

sections.label: Notice period for parents and staff
sections.summary: Asks what notice period parents and staff will be given should such an incident arise.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: What is the notice period that will be given to the parents and staff should such an incident arise?

sections.label: Audit of ECDC not compulsory
sections.summary: Notes the positives in the Bill, seeks clarifications, and states that an audit of an ECDC may not be compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the many positives in the Bill, I would like to seek several clarifications from the Minister, many of which have actually been raised already.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, it appears that an audit of an ECDC may not be compulsory.

sections.label: Security deposit for all licensees
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to clarify why a security deposit is not made compulsory for all licensees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify why we are not making the provision of a security deposit compulsory for all licensees?

sections.label: Minimum notice period and MOE kindergartens
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to specify the minimum notice period for the licensee to issue such a notice, and notes MOE kindergartens are not regulated under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister specify the minimum notice period for the licensee to issue such a notice?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, I understand that MOE kindergartens are not regulated under this Bill.

sections.label: Start date for new policies
sections.summary: The speaker hopes new policies announced by Josephine Teo and Tan Chuan-Jin start at the beginning of the year, not immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As always, children never listen and so I pray that for any new policies that Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo and Minister Tan Chuan-Jin will be announcing shortly, the start date will be the beginning of this year and not with immediate effect from the date of the announcement.

sections.label: Regulating all pre-schools
sections.summary: The speaker supports regulating all pre-schools under a single framework with requirements on registration, admission and fee increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet all of them must meet certain health, safety and teaching standards to ensure that the children are well-cared for and ready for our primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support regulating all pre-schools under a single regulatory framework for consistency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new framework will further safeguard the interests of our children and their parents through requirements, such as getting operators to clearly state their registration and admission processes and giving parents sufficient notice if they decide to increase their fees.

sections.label: More unannounced audits urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to conduct unannounced audits at least twice yearly due to longer licence tenure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Due to the proposed longer licence tenure, I urge the Ministry to conduct unannounced audits more regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider increasing the frequency to at least twice yearly to ensure that centres maintain their standards?

sections.label: Basic curriculum and pedagogy baseline
sections.summary: The speaker says MOE and MSF setting a basic curriculum and regulated baseline would give children a basic standard of quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I think that aggressive interventions and heavy regulations in the early childhood sector are not necessary at this point in time and the element of choice for parents is important, it would undeniably be useful for MOE and MSF to set a basic curriculum and establish a regulated baseline pedagogy and a certain level of quality to ensure that our children, regardless of socio-economic background, have the opportunity to enjoy a certain basic standard of quality early childhood education.

sections.label: Approval for ECDC duties
sections.summary: The speaker says the clause 23 amendment requiring approval for persons performing duties at ECDCs enhances quality by ensuring qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendment to clause 23, where approval must explicitly be sought for persons who perform duties at ECDCs, will further enhance the quality of early childhood education by ensuring that all teachers and allied educators have the relevant qualifications and skills to teach our preschoolers.

sections.label: Incentives for mid-career switchers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests giving incentives to mid-career switchers to attend mid-career conversion courses that induct them into the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In particular, I would like to suggest that incentives be given to mid-career switchers to attend mid-career conversion courses that induct them quickly into the sector.

sections.label: Clause 29 third-party providers
sections.summary: Amendments to clause 29 impose regulatory requirements on ECDCs deploying third-party education service providers, and the speaker asks about F&B vendors and a certification framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments to clause 29 that stipulates the regulatory requirements imposed on ECDCs when they deploy third-party education service providers are a step in the right directions towards raising safety and quality standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In instances such as these, it is important that third-party education service providers be thoroughly assessed for their suitability and whether they have the right level of competency to offer such services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It would disastrous if classes, such as gymnastics, are being conducted by untrained third-party providers who do not have the right level of competency or awareness about safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As an addendum to the Bill, I hope that the Government can clarify whether clause 29 will be applied to vendors who provide non-educational service to ECDCs, for example, food and beverage (F&B) vendors who supply food to the centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Going further, would the Government consider mandating vendors that supply food to children in preschools and primary schools to provide a well-balanced diet that is suitable for young children?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It might thus be fruitful for the Health Promotion Board and MOE to jointly work on a regulatory and certification framework, together with MSF, to assess vendors that provide F&B to preschools, childcare centres and kindergartens, so that our children can enjoy nutritious and well-balanced meals in schools.

sections.label: Early childhood component and ECDA
sections.summary: The early childhood component is vital, which is why ECDA was set up as an independent agency jointly overseen by MOE and MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: What is clear is this − the early childhood component for our children is vital, which is why we set up ECDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It is an independent agency but jointly overseen by MOE and MSF.

sections.label: Two-year involved process
sections.summary: The process has taken over two years because it is a very involved process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The process has taken over two years, because it is a very involved process.

sections.label: Standards for preschool affordability
sections.summary: Some can bridge the gap and run, others struggle, so a level of standard in affordability, accessibility and quality is important to level children up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Some are able to bridge that and carry on and run, but others struggle and might not be able to bridge that gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Hence, it is important to impose, to some degree, a level of standard in terms of affordability, accessibility and quality of preschools, to make sure that as many children are levelled up as much as possible.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot with families
sections.summary: KidSTART is aimed at working with children from this segment and is in a pilot stage with 1,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Importantly, KidSTART is aimed at working with children from this segment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It is in a pilot stage with 1,000 families.

sections.label: ECDA initiatives for professionals
sections.summary: In recent years, ECDA has rolled out a range of initiatives to attract, retain and develop good early childhood professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In recent years, ECDA has rolled out a range of initiatives to attract, retain and develop good early childhood professionals.

sections.label: Subsidised training places response
sections.summary: Subsidised training places, work-and-study arrangements and ECDA Training Awards have drawn an encouraging response, with higher early childhood polytechnic enrolment and more mid-career entrants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Through the ramping up of subsidised training places, including the work-and-study arrangements for mid-career entrants and ECDA's Training Awards for aspiring teachers, we are seeing a very encouraging response, such as higher enrolment numbers in the early childhood polytechnic courses and more mid-career entrants joining the sector.

sections.label: ECDA recognises prior learning
sections.summary: When in-service educators apply for training courses, ECDA recognises their prior learning and working experiences beyond paper qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: When in-service educators apply for training courses, ECDA recognises their prior learning and working experiences beyond their paper qualifications.

sections.label: Nutrition and physical activity guidelines
sections.summary: ECDA will specify detailed nutritional requirements, including no sugary drinks or deep-fried food, and increase daily physical activity to an hour for full-day programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As announced by the NurtureSG Taskforce last week, ECDA will specify more detailed nutritional requirements to ensure that children receive nutritious, balanced and varied meals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We urge families to also look out for these guidelines to follow them at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: These include not allowing centres to serve sugary drinks and deep-fried food, and catering for the regular provision of fruits and calcium-rich food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The physical activity time for full-day programmes will also be increased to an hour daily, up from half an hour today, and half an hour at least to be conducted outdoors and more, if you can.

sections.label: Kindergartens licence application period
sections.summary: Kindergartens will be given up to a year after gazetting of regulations under the new Act, expected around late 2017 or early 2018, to obtain licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In addition, kindergartens will be given up to a year after the gazetting of regulations under the new Act, which is expected to be about late 2017 or early 2018, for them to obtain their licences.

sections.label: Longer three-year licence tenure
sections.summary: A new longer three-year licence tenure is intended to reduce administrative costs of centres with consistently good regulatory track records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For example, we have a new longer three-year licence tenure which is intended to reduce the administrative costs of centres with consistently good regulatory track records.

sections.label: Centres prepared, no added requirements
sections.summary: Many centres are well-prepared, partly due to earlier ECDA funding for air purifiers during haze, and no increase in staffing and space requirements is planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In fact, as a result of the effort in the past one to two years, many centres are already well-prepared for this, especially as ECDA has earlier provided funding support to centres to procure air purifiers during severe haze episodes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We also do not plan to increase regulatory requirements around staffing numbers and space allocation, which are the main cost factors for centres.

sections.label: ECDA practices and kindergarten funding
sections.summary: ECDA can share good practices with the sector, and funding support was extended to not-for-profit kindergartens for staff immunisation and minor renovation costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: ECDA's advantage is that, because of their oversight over the rest of the sector, ECDA can bring into play many good practices which can be imparted to other players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We have also extended funding support to the not-for-profit kindergartens to help them defray staff immunisation and also minor renovation costs.

sections.label: Quality targets and fee caps
sections.summary: AOP and POP centres have quality targets and fee caps, and centres must give early notice of fee increases and explain them to parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Today, there are quality targets and fee caps on the AOP and POP centres, which serve nearly half of the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: While the Bill will not determine the fees of different preschools − this will be addressed separately − we will continue to require centres to provide sufficient early notification of any plans to increase fees and explain the fee increase to parents.

sections.label: Publishing incidental charges
sections.summary: Following parent feedback, ECDA is looking into requiring centres to publish incidental charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Following feedback from parents, ECDA is also looking into requiring centres to publish incidental charges.

sections.label: No designated compliance staff required
sections.summary: In reply to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, operators are not required to employ designated administrative or compliance staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To Mr Gan Thiam Poh's query, we do not require operators to employ designated administrative or compliance staff.

sections.label: MOE kindergartens meet ECDA requirements
sections.summary: MOE kindergartens will fulfil ECDA's requirements, along with the rest of the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: MOE kindergartens will fulfil ECDA's requirements, along with the rest of the industry.

sections.label: Closure advance notification period
sections.summary: ECDA is studying the advance notification period for centres intending to cease operations, which happens from time to time for various reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With regard to Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Louis Ng's questions on closure arrangements, ECDA is studying the advance notification period for centres which intend to cease their operations, which will happen from time to time for various reasons.

sections.label: Emergency directions and penalties
sections.summary: ECDA intends to issue directions under clause 17 only for emergency cases, with non-compliance a criminal offence liable to a $10,000 fine and 12 months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To Ms Thanaletchimi's question on directions for emergencies, ECDA intends to issue directions under clause 17 only for emergency cases, such as hazardous haze episodes, where children's safety is at stake and centres need to act swiftly to safeguard their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As such, it is a criminal offence for any non-compliance, liable up to a fine of $10,000 and imprisonment of 12 months, as determined by the Courts.

sections.label: Security deposit for poor centres
sections.summary: The security deposit applies to a small number of centres with poor regulatory track records as assurance of their commitment to improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With regard to the security deposit, this is something that Mr Louis Ng raised, I have also touched on the application of the security deposit as well as the proposed amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are applying the security deposit on a small number of centres with poor regulatory track records as a form of assurance from them on their commitment to improve, while recognising that the majority of our sector, by and large, is performing well.

sections.label: Bill raises early childhood quality
sections.summary: The Bill is a milestone in raising early childhood care and education quality and complements Government initiatives on quality, accessibility and affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I will also be talking about some of these concerns during the COS debate, and we will have other debates on some of those topics in this House in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This Bill is a very important milestone in our journey in raising the quality of early childhood care and education in Singapore, for our children, our families and, from a national perspective, for our future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This Bill will complement the many initiatives that the Government has introduced to enhance the quality, accessibility and affordability of early childhood development services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This will ensure that every child, regardless of his or her background, can have a good start in life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It is important for us to ensure that every child has that good start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It will also further strengthen our commitment to make Singapore a good place to raise families.

sections.label: No significant cost increases expected
sections.summary: The Government does not anticipate significant cost increases as a result of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: From one perspective, one could naturally imagine how this could lead to higher compliance cost and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We do not anticipate there to be significant cost increases as a result of this Bill.

sections.label: Kindergartens get one-year transition
sections.summary: ECDA will give kindergartens an additional one year to transit, and the Bill is not expected to translate into higher fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For kindergartens, for example, ECDA will provide more time for them to transit and, as I mentioned, they will be given an additional one year from the time that the Bill kicks in formally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We do not expect the compliance cost to be onerous and, therefore, we are not expecting the Bill to translate into higher fees.

sections.label: ECDA studies lower operating costs
sections.summary: ECDA is studying ways to lower operating costs, such as more flexible manpower deployment allowing operational staff to assist trained teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: ECDA is also studying other ways to lower cost of operations, for example, providing more flexibility in manpower deployment, something that we will be looking at to support the sector, by allowing operational staff to assist trained teachers and so on.
